method: Read-only source inspection; no application execution, provider calls, exploit execution, dependency advisory lookup, or network activity. Only this audit artifact was written. Findings refer to baseline source; parent-agent remediation is not verified here.

findings.title: Auto-execution bypasses human-review requirements and rejected decisions
findings.evidence: Policy computes requiresHumanReview but does not include its negation in auto_execute_allowed. runAction accepts any non-executed status when auto allowance is true, including rejected. High/critical items also become eligible when the configured ceiling permits them.
findings.prerequisites: Operator has enabled global/source auto-actions and a policy permits auto-execution; an agent or operator invokes run on an affected action.
findings.impact: Outbound sends/comments or local mutations can execute despite an explicit human gate or rejection.
findings.counterevidence: Default global auto-actions are off and default policy blocks direct sending. No autonomous polling executor invokes runAction by itself.
findings.fix: Require absence of all human-review conditions for automatic execution; make rejection terminal and enforce lifecycle transitions. Preserve explicit human approval for otherwise allowed actions.

findings.title: Rule action blocks and policy confidence thresholds are descriptive only
findings.evidence: applyRules ignores blocked_actions entirely. evaluatePolicy reads only policy-level blocked_actions and never reads confidence_threshold. Defaults and documentation advertise these controls.
findings.prerequisites: An operator permits an action globally while relying on a matching rule to block it, or enables auto-actions while relying on confidence_threshold.
findings.impact: Configured safety constraints do not constrain execution.
findings.counterevidence: Default sending block independently prevents direct sends; risk ceilings still apply to auto-execution.
findings.fix: Carry trusted matched-rule blocks into policy evaluation, including auto_execute, and enforce finite confidence thresholds for automatic execution.

findings.title: Nonmatching policies silently authorize through first-policy fallback
findings.evidence: A failed policies.find falls back to policies[0], even when that policy explicitly scopes itself to a different source/category.
findings.prerequisites: Deployment uses scoped policies without a matching catch-all.
findings.impact: An action outside the configured policy scope can inherit unrelated allowances.
findings.counterevidence: Default policy explicitly matches all sources/categories, so default behavior is unaffected.
findings.fix: Return a blocked result when no policy applies; preserve explicit wildcard behavior.

findings.title: Insecure-localhost URL exception accepts external hosts
findings.evidence: startsWith('http://localhost') and startsWith('http://127.0.0.1') accept external suffix hosts such as localhost.attacker.example; fetch sends the selected API key as a bearer credential.
findings.prerequisites: KUJO_AI_SDK_ALLOW_INSECURE_LOCALHOST=true and a misleading configured base URL, with AI enabled and an API key present.
findings.impact: API key and inbound content can cross an unencrypted external connection despite a localhost-only exception.
findings.counterevidence: Configuration is operator-controlled; exception is disabled by default. This is not an unauthenticated remote settings write.
findings.fix: Parse URL and compare exact normalized hostname, protocol, username/password, query and fragment; use the parsed normalized value consistently.

findings.title: Secret-free output omits supported inline secret fields
findings.evidence: sanitizeSource masks token/api_token but not supported config.signing_secret. Default backup exclusions skip .env and secrets directories but copy sources.json verbatim, including supported inline token, api_token and signing_secret.
findings.prerequisites: A source uses a supported legacy inline secret and an operator shares default config export or a backup created with includeSecrets=false.
findings.impact: Webhook signing/authentication secrets or outbound API tokens leak through apparently secret-free artifacts.
findings.counterevidence: Recommended secret references do not embed values; dashboard source reads require its operator token.
findings.fix: Sanitize all supported inline credential fields in source output and secret-excluding backups, leaving reference fields intact; test preservation under explicit includeSecrets.

findings.title: Proposed rules are active before approval
findings.evidence: rules propose saves a rule with status proposed; applyRules iterates it without checking status. The separate rules approve command has no effect on eligibility.
findings.prerequisites: Operator or agent proposes an inbound-derived rule and later classifies another matching item before review.
findings.impact: Unreviewed inbound-derived classification and routing affect future items.
findings.counterevidence: Proposal creation itself requires local operator execution; proposed rules do not lower existing risk and do not currently contain action blocks.
findings.fix: Skip explicitly nonapproved rules while preserving existing legacy rules with no status.

findings.title: Restore verifies a different read from the archive it consumes and mutates before complete validation
findings.evidence: restoreBackup verifies one decompression then decompresses again without validating that second object. Validation also accepts '.' and duplicate or file/parent-conflicting paths when their content checksums match. With force, target is deleted before extraction discovers such conflicts. Decompressed bytes are unbounded.
findings.prerequisites: Operator restores a malformed/untrusted backup, or another local actor can replace it between reads. Force replacement is required for destruction of an existing target.
findings.impact: Unexpected unverified files can be restored; malformed archives can destroy a target then fail; compressed inputs can exhaust memory.
findings.counterevidence: Lexical safeJoin prevents ordinary ../ writes outside the target. Archive is local operator-selected, not accepted by a network endpoint.
findings.fix: Read once with a decompressed-byte bound, validate strict entry shape and canonical unique nonconflicting file paths, stage the full store before replacement, then restore exactly the validated bytes.

findings.title: Concurrent action runs can duplicate outbound side effects
findings.evidence: Each run reads status, performs external execution, and only then saves executed. Two concurrent requests can both read approved and send/comment. Automatic budget counters use read-modify-write after execution and can similarly overrun caps.
findings.prerequisites: Two authenticated calls or local processes run the same action or simultaneously consume the remaining auto budget.
findings.impact: Duplicate outward messages and exceeded configured rate limits.
findings.counterevidence: Sequential reruns return the executed record. API is authenticated; this does not independently give outsiders run access.
findings.fix: Serialize execution and budget reservations per store across supported processes, re-read status under lock, and explicitly handle crash ambiguity without claiming exactly-once network delivery.

findings.title: File-drop symlinks cross the inbound filesystem boundary
findings.evidence: syncFileSource uses stat, which follows symlinks, then readFile. A drop-folder entry named with a supported extension can point outside the folder and be imported as inbound content.
findings.prerequisites: A less-trusted actor can add symlinks to the configured drop directory but cannot read a file the Intake account can read.
findings.impact: Intake copies the target into raw/items and can submit its content to an enabled AI provider.
findings.counterevidence: Directory path is operator configured; exploitation requires writable local/drop filesystem access, not merely a JSON payload.
findings.fix: Reject symlink entries and use no-follow file handles with regular-file checks; bound file size before buffering.

hardening_observations: readRaw and attachment downloads enforce lexical containment, not realpath containment. A local actor must be able to plant store symlinks for an escape; no inbound adapter accepts arbitrary quarantine_path, so this was not elevated to a remote vulnerability.

IMAP runtime construction does not call validateEmailConfig and accepts secure:false, unlike SMTP runtime guard. Dependency STARTTLS behavior was not audited, so plaintext password disclosure is not claimed. Enforce documented encrypted-mail policy at the runtime boundary.

Atomic write temporary names use pid and millisecond timestamp and are opened nonexclusively; simultaneous writes to the same path may collide. Index read-modify-write can lose concurrent entries. These are concurrency integrity issues independent of authentication.

Dashboard action editing preserves approved status and approval metadata after body/type changes; reset approval when execution-relevant content changes. This requires existing operator access, not an unauthenticated attacker.

Dashboard rotation updates sessionStorage but api() closes over an immutable initial token, so the current UI starts receiving 401 after rotation until reload. This is a confirmed availability bug, not an auth bypass.
No dependency vulnerability claims were made because this review was offline and did not inspect advisory data.
counterevidence: Dashboard has bearer/custom-header authentication, random local default token, HTTPS and minimum explicit-token checks for nonlocal binding, no cookies or permissive CORS, and frame-denying headers.
Inbound dashboard fields use textContent; raw inbound HTML is not inserted as markup. HTML sinks are restricted to package-owned SVG icons.
Webhook receivers bind loopback, cap request bodies at 1 MiB, and authenticate; Slack checks HMAC and timestamp skew. GitHub supports HMAC with explicit token compatibility.
Storage record IDs reject slash traversal. Quarantined attachment names derive from safe IDs and hashes, and downloads have a 25 MiB size check.
Email headers strip CR/LF, keychain invocation uses execFileSync with an argument array, and no inbound content is evaluated as shell or JavaScript.
coverage_limitations: All runtime source files and executable support scripts were inspected. Test files, dependency internals and every documentation page were not fully audited. No stronger end-to-end or exploit validation is claimed.
